items.title: Shorter, clearer texts
items.detail: Screens, messages and the manual were rewritten to be shorter and more direct, in every language.

items.title: Mods install from the site
items.detail: To install a mod, open its page on the site, signed in, and click Install in JayV; the app syncs right away. Uninstalls wait in the list, with Undo, until you save.

items.title: Only the essential mods come installed
items.detail: In a new environment, only the essential mods are installed. Install the agents you use; what you already have stays as it is.

items.title: Essential mods in their own tab
items.detail: In Settings › Mods, installed mods are split into two tabs, Installed and Essentials. Ctrl+K opens either one.

items.title: What syncs shows up by itself
items.detail: Changes from other computers or the site now show up on their own.

items.title: No flood of notifications on a new computer
items.detail: A new computer no longer gets a flood of notifications for past answers.

items.title: An answer no longer blanks the window
items.detail: Some links no longer blank the window. If a screen fails to draw, it shows what went wrong and a Try again button.

items.title: General chat counts every clone in the folder
items.detail: The general chat now counts every clone in the organization folder.

items.title: Saving mods keeps what changed elsewhere
items.detail: Saving Settings › Mods now applies only what you changed, keeping changes made elsewhere.

items.title: /mcp no longer waits for the running request
items.detail: /mcp drafts now come right away, without waiting for other chats.

items.title: Following the agent in the editor does not freeze the window
items.detail: Opening a changed file in your editor no longer freezes the window.

items.title: Refusing a plan no longer approves it
items.detail: Refusing a plan or asking for changes no longer approves it; Jev treats the message as a new request.

items.title: Late questions no longer lock the message box
items.detail: A question found late no longer locks the message box after you've already sent another message.

items.title: The mode you pick during a request stays
items.detail: The mode you pick while a request runs stays when it finishes.

items.title: Clearing a chat stops its request
items.detail: Clearing or deleting a chat now stops its request, closes any pending question and cancels any wait.

items.title: "It didn't work" counts only for its own request
items.detail: “It didn't work” now affects only the request where you said it.

items.title: An organization's general chat and its repositories take turns
items.detail: A project inside another project's folder now waits for it, so two agents never write to the same repository at once.

items.title: Stop no longer gets stuck
items.detail: If stopping a request fails, the Stop button comes back so you can try again.

items.title: The code panel, with repositories
items.detail: The Code button opens a panel with two tabs: Files, with the request's changes and diffs, and Repositories, with the git status of each repository in the chat's folder. It also says why git didn't respond.

items.title: General chats in the Chats item of the side menu
items.detail: In an organization's environment, general chats are under Chats in the side menu, which opens and closes the list.

items.title: Every mod has its icon
items.detail: Each mod has its own icon in Settings › Mods, in the agent tabs and on the site.

items.title: Fewer mods installed by default
items.detail: Fewer mods are installed on first sign-in; the rest wait for whoever wants them. Mods you already have stay as they are.

items.title: What's new waits for the update
items.detail: What's new now waits for the update screens to close before opening.

items.title: REA: reverse engineering, picked by Jev
items.detail: Mods can bring skills that Jev picks for the request. The first is REA, for reverse engineering apps, binaries, websites and processes. Turn on Approve MCP servers in an agent's tab so it can use REA's tools.

items.title: Every mod has its own page on the site
items.detail: Each mod has a page on the site with what it does, how to install it and how to use it, with screenshots in your language. The book button in Settings › Mods opens it.

items.title: Requests resume when the usage limit comes back
items.detail: When an agent hits its usage limit and no other agent can take over, the request is resent automatically when the limit resets, even if the app was closed. You can resume now or stop waiting. Turn it off in Settings › Jev.

items.title: Auto mode now plans and then builds
items.detail: In Auto mode, a plan with no open questions is approved and the chat moves to Development. Planning stays read-only when pinned.

items.title: Commands covered by an always-on permission show as ticked
items.detail: When the organization keeps a permission always on, the commands it covers show as checked and locked.

items.title: Turning on an agent without any model now says so
items.detail: An agent that is on with all models off now shows a notice, and the error says to turn on a model. Loading models also works with unsaved changes.

items.title: The organization is no longer blamed when no agent is on
items.detail: A failed request now blames the organization's policy only when the policy is the real cause; otherwise it says what's missing.

items.title: Chat permissions the organization keeps always on
items.detail: Each chat permission can now be Free, Always on or Blocked by the organization. Always-on ones are switched on and locked in the organization's chats.

items.title: Chat permissions of the organization
items.detail: Owners and maintainers choose on the site which chat permissions (commands, Git, network) members can turn on. Blocked ones show as disabled.

items.title: System admins get every feature
items.detail: System administrators get every feature on any plan.

items.title: The admin can turn any feature on or off, core ones included
items.detail: The administrator can now turn any feature off for everyone or leave it out of a plan, core ones included.

items.title: Plan prices in several currencies and by country
items.detail: Paid plans can have prices in several currencies, each for specific countries. The Plans page opens in your country's currency, and you can switch it.

items.title: Plans managed on the site
items.detail: Plans are created on the site and published for sale automatically, with their prices.

items.title: Mods have their own section in the Documentation
items.detail: Mod pages moved to their own Mods section in the documentation.

items.title: Essential mods
items.detail: The app's features are now essential mods: they always stay installed and on. LLM engines and agents can still be turned off and uninstalled. Your plan still decides which features you have.

items.title: Mods for everything
items.detail: Settings › Mods is now a mod manager: each mod has a version and an author, can add several things and depend on other mods, and you install, turn on, turn off and uninstall it. Your choices follow the environment to your other computers.

items.title: Features are mods too
items.detail: App features are now mods too, so you can turn off what you don't use in Settings › Mods. Ready-made mods are also available to install.

items.title: Create mods on the site
items.detail: Mods are now created on the site, where you create, edit and delete them for each environment. They reach the app through sync; API keys are still entered only on this computer.

items.title: LLM integrations are mods
items.detail: Agents are now mods, listed in Settings › Mods. Create mod connects another LLM, a command-line program or an API, with its own tab and models.

items.title: General chats beside the side menu
items.detail: In an organization's environment, general chats got their own column beside the side menu; + starts a new one.

items.title: Settings change only when you save
items.detail: Nothing in Settings takes effect until you click Save settings. Changed items are marked Not saved, and Discard drops them.

items.title: Organization projects are deleted on the site
items.detail: Organization projects are deleted on the site by an owner or maintainer, and they leave every member's app.

items.title: Settings without the organization's MCP and skills
items.detail: Settings › MCP and Skills list only your own servers and skills. The organization's are in its environment.

items.title: No scrolling outside the content
items.detail: The window no longer scrolls or bounces as a whole; only each screen's content scrolls.

items.title: Long tutorial steps in parts
items.detail: Long tutorial steps are split into short parts, with markers showing where you are.

items.title: The organization heads the Projects page
items.detail: In an organization's environment, the Projects page shows the organization at the top, with its Open chat button.

items.title: Organizations through the environment selector
items.detail: You open an organization by choosing its environment under the logo. Invitations are answered in the notifications, and organizations are managed on the site.

items.title: The organization's own menu
items.detail: In an organization's environment, the side menu shows only that organization and its tabs.

items.title: Cleaner update check on opening
items.detail: The update check on startup now shows only “Checking for updates…”.

items.title: Notifications on the site too
items.detail: The site now has the same notifications bell as the app for invitations and organization changes. Reading one marks it read in both.

items.title: Manual of environments mentions the loading screen
items.detail: The manual now says that switching environments shows a loading screen.

items.title: Switching environment shows a loading screen
items.detail: Switching environments shows a loading screen until the data arrives, without checking for updates.

items.title: Pending invites in the Members tab
items.detail: Owners and maintainers see pending invites below the members.

items.title: Switching environment no longer shows a sign-in error
items.detail: Switching to an organization's environment no longer shows a sign-in error.

items.title: Usage by environment
items.detail: Statistics show which environment the usage belongs to.

items.title: Separate environments
items.detail: Your personal projects and each organization have their own environment, with separate projects, chats, notes, usage and settings. Switch under the logo or with Ctrl+K. Your profile, language, theme and plan stay the same.

items.title: Organization page like the site
items.detail: The organization's tabs now sit in a vertical column, with new MCP and Skills tabs listing what the organization provides.

items.title: Every feature in the admin list
items.detail: MCP servers, skills, skills.sh search, the Kilo Code agent, API models and find in conversation can now be set per plan. Existing plans keep all of them.

items.title: One back button everywhere
items.detail: All back buttons now use the same arrow, in light and dark themes.

items.title: Install skills from skills.sh
items.detail: Settings › Skills has a skills.sh section: search and install a skill with one click. Organizations can also install skills for all members on the site.

items.title: Chat permissions count in Auto mode
items.detail: In Auto mode, a request with chat permissions now goes to Development so the agent can use them. A pinned Planning mode stays read-only.

items.title: Saving settings takes effect right away
items.detail: Saved settings now apply from the next request, without restarting. A running request finishes with the old ones.

items.title: The chosen skill reaches parallel agents
items.detail: The skill Jev picks now reaches every agent in a request split into parallel parts.

items.title: MCP servers ready to use
items.detail: Common MCP servers now come ready in Settings › MCP, and you can turn them off, edit or remove them. In an organization's chats, its servers take precedence over yours with the same name.

items.title: MCP servers for every agent
items.detail: MCP servers now reach every agent that has “Approve MCP servers” on in its tab (off by default). Ctrl+K has a command to switch it per agent.

items.title: “Go ahead with the plan” now builds
items.detail: In Auto mode, asking to continue with the existing plan now goes straight to Development with the whole plan.

items.title: Quota guard for every agent
items.detail: Agents close to their plan limit aren't used, and very long runs stop with a message in the chat, to protect your quota.

items.title: Find in the conversation (Ctrl+F)
items.detail: Ctrl+F (⌘F on Mac) searches the open chat and highlights matches. Enter and Shift+Enter move between them; Esc closes.

items.title: Browser shortcuts are blocked
items.detail: Browser shortcuts like reload, zoom and print no longer work in the app. Copy, paste, undo and the app's own shortcuts still do.

items.title: The code panel says what it is watching
items.detail: The code panel shows which folder it's watching, or that it isn't watching any, and finds your code editor in more places.

items.title: Permissions last for the whole chat
items.detail: Permissions you turn on now last for the whole chat until you turn them off. What the organization blocks still applies.

items.title: Bell and help next to the logo
items.detail: The notifications bell and the help button moved to the top of the sidebar.

items.title: Replies always in your language
items.detail: Every request now reminds the model of your language, so replies stay in it.

items.title: Code and files recognized in every reply
items.detail: Replies are formatted as they're written, and file paths and code blocks are recognized in more formats.

items.title: Models start turned off
items.detail: New models now start turned off; turn on the ones you want in each agent's settings. Models already on stay on.

items.title: A spinner on every loading screen
items.detail: Loading screens now show a spinner.

items.title: No Skip button on the update screen
items.detail: The update check at startup no longer has a Skip button. Without a network, the app opens after 10 seconds.

items.title: Command permissions of the organization
items.detail: Owners and maintainers choose on the site which commands agents can never run in the organization's projects. Blocked commands show as disabled in the chat's Permissions.

items.title: Example env files stay readable to agents
items.detail: Example env files like .env.example are no longer blocked, while real .env files stay protected.

items.title: The progress panel follows the latest step
items.detail: The progress panel scrolls to the latest step automatically. If you scroll up, it stays put and offers a button to jump back.

items.title: Official icons and checked integrations
items.detail: The new agents use their official icons, and their default settings now match their documentation.

items.title: Three new agents
items.detail: Three new agents in Settings: a command-line agent that edits the project and two API gateways that answer with text only. Organizations can allow or block each one.

items.title: Tutorials for every feature
items.detail: Each screen has a guided tour that opens on your first visit. Open it again from the help button (?), Ctrl+K or Settings › App › Tutorials.

items.title: Updates itself when it opens
items.detail: When the app opens, it installs any new version and restarts. Turn this off in Settings › App › Version or with Ctrl+K.

items.title: MCP servers and skills of the organization
items.detail: Owners and maintainers set up the organization's MCP servers and skills on the site, and every member gets them in the app, read-only, in the organization's projects.

items.title: Settings tabs on the left
items.detail: Settings tabs now sit in a column on the left that stays in view as you scroll.

items.title: Skills that Jev chooses for you
items.detail: Install skills in Settings › Skills. For each request, Jev picks the skill that fits, if any, and the chat shows when one was used.

items.title: Replies in the app's language
items.detail: Replies sometimes came in another language. Your chosen language is now kept and sent with every request.

items.title: Every screen is reachable from Ctrl+K
items.detail: The command palette (Ctrl+K) now reaches every screen and its main actions.

items.title: General chats of the organization, kept apart
items.detail: Chats that work on all of an organization's repositories now have their own General chats section. They're also in the command palette (Ctrl+K).

items.title: Windows updates no longer get stuck closing the app
items.detail: The Windows installer now waits for the app to close and ends any leftover process instead of failing.

items.title: MCP servers for your agents
items.detail: Settings › MCP lists the servers your agents get on each request. Add one by hand, paste a configuration, or type /mcp in a chat; nothing is saved until you check it.

items.title: Permissions for the next message
items.detail: Next to the mode, Permissions lets you allow commands, Git writes and network access for your next message.

items.title: A blocked command now asks you
items.detail: When a permission blocks the agent, you're asked whether to run the command, deny it or always allow it in the project.

items.title: Resize the progress panel
items.detail: Drag the edge of the progress panel to resize it; double-click to reset. The width is remembered.

items.title: Approving a plan in Auto mode now starts the change
items.detail: In Auto mode, approving a plan from the same chat now runs it in Development, as long as it passes the gate and isn't destructive.

items.title: A safer GitHub connection
items.detail: Signing in with GitHub and connecting repositories now use a GitHub App that reaches only the repositories you choose. Organizations connected before must reconnect.

items.title: Answers say what was really checked
items.detail: Answers are no longer marked as passed just because they followed the rules. What was checked shows what the app verified, what a model only said, and what wasn't verified.

items.title: Repositories come from the site
items.detail: The owner links the organization's repositories on the site, and they show up in the app automatically.

items.title: Find clones looks at the whole folder
items.detail: Find clones searches the whole organization folder and compares it with the organization's repositories: what's there, what's missing and what doesn't belong.

items.title: Your profile photo, whatever way you sign in
items.detail: The photo you set on the site now shows in the app, however you sign in.

items.title: Documentation and release notes on the site
items.detail: Every feature and command has a page in the documentation on the site, and the release notes list what each version brought.

items.title: Updates through the app's own server
items.detail: The app now checks for and downloads updates through its own server.

items.title: Requests from different projects run at the same time
items.detail: If your plan allows it, chats from different projects run at the same time. Requests in the same project still run one at a time.

items.title: The plan appears while it is written
items.detail: When a plan is written first, each line shows in the progress panel as it's written.

items.title: Lighter loading of your chats
items.detail: Chats load faster: each conversation loads only when you open it.

items.title: Progress panel beside the chat
items.detail: Request progress moved to a panel beside the chat, one step per line. The panel can be collapsed.

items.title: Stop replaces Send while a request runs
items.detail: While a request runs, Send turns into Stop. Enter still queues a new message.

items.title: Live follow in your editor answers right away
items.detail: Choosing an editor in the code panel now opens the current file right away, and the panel says when no editor is found.

items.title: Protections your plan keeps on
items.detail: Core protections such as the gates, secret redaction, protected files, agent sessions, the context cache and adaptive routing are part of every plan. A plan can also keep an optional feature on, and its switch shows why.

items.title: Stop a request
items.detail: Stop ends the running request; what was already answered stays in the chat. Queued requests can be removed, and every request stops at a time limit you set in Settings › Jev.

items.title: Protected files stay protected
items.detail: Files in your protected list can't be read or edited, and any change to them is held at the exit gate.

items.title: The second opinion arrives after the answer
items.detail: The second opinion now runs after the answer, only for medium and complex requests, and the next request doesn't wait for it.

items.title: Requests start faster
items.detail: Requests start faster: agents aren't reloaded every time, indexes are kept, and only changed files are read again.

items.title: Signed-out agents are skipped
items.detail: Agents that aren't signed in are skipped, and checking an agent in Settings shows whether it's signed in.

items.title: The queue keeps going without the server
items.detail: With a valid session, requests keep running even when the server can't be reached.

items.title: Agent command lines that always work
items.detail: Agents no longer wait for approvals nobody can give, and planning, review and chat titles no longer leave sessions behind.

items.title: Answers appear as they're written
items.detail: Answers now appear on screen as they're written, without slowing down the window.

items.title: The gatehouse no longer holds a request for minutes
items.detail: The gatehouse waits only a few seconds before deciding locally, so requests are no longer held for minutes.

items.title: Steadier conversations with the agents
items.detail: Conversations with agents are steadier: expired sessions restart, unusual text no longer breaks requests, and the backup agent takes over when needed.

items.title: The project index follows .gitignore
items.detail: The project index follows .gitignore, so ignored files, virtual environments and build folders stay out of the context.

items.title: Deleting or clearing a chat answers at once
items.detail: Clearing or deleting a chat or project no longer waits for another chat's request.

items.title: jayv bench measures rounds until done
items.detail: jayv bench now runs task files and compares how many requests and how much money each side needed to finish.

items.title: The build gets the whole plan
items.detail: When you plan and then ask to implement, the building agent gets the whole plan.

items.title: "It didn't work" no longer retries the same way
items.detail: After “it didn't work”, the agent checks its last change and reproduces the failure before trying again.

items.title: Searches in your language, cheaper titles and honest savings
items.detail: Requests in other languages now also find code written in English, and a resent blocked request no longer counts as savings.

items.title: A chat stays on its model, so the agent resumes
items.detail: A chat stays on its first model so the agent can resume its session, unless a complex request needs a bigger one. Turn it off in Settings › Jev.

items.title: Agent sessions survive a restart
items.detail: Agent sessions are kept on this computer for a day, so restarting the app doesn't start chats from scratch.

items.title: The gatehouse asks you itself, before any agent runs
items.detail: When a request is cleared with reservations, the gatehouse asks you directly: send as written, send a rewritten version, or complete the request.

items.title: Follow-ups keep the pass of the request they continue
items.detail: Short follow-ups like “go ahead” or “it still fails” keep the gatehouse verdict of the request they continue.

items.title: Why an agent starts over
items.detail: The app now records why an agent starts a new session instead of resuming, to reduce the rounds needed to finish a request.

items.title: Several questions from the agent, one step at a time
items.detail: When the agent asks several questions, they come one at a time with Previous and Next, and the answers are sent together at the end.

items.title: Collapse the agent's questions
items.detail: The agent's question panel can be collapsed to one line so you can read the chat.

items.title: Agent network access works again
items.detail: The Network access switch works again in the agent's sandbox settings, and applies whenever it writes to the project.

items.title: Organizations managed on the site
items.detail: Creating organizations, inviting members and the LLM policy moved to the dashboard on the site.

items.title: Organization settings on the site
items.detail: Renaming, leaving and deleting an organization moved to the dashboard on the site.

items.title: Account settings on the site
items.detail: Personal data, password, authenticator app and linked accounts moved to the dashboard on the site. The Profile page keeps your level, activity and agent quotas.

items.title: Administration only on the site
items.detail: Administration left the app: features, plans and users are managed in the dashboard on the site.

items.title: The agent no longer stays read-only after planning
items.detail: After switching from Planning to Development, the agent no longer stays read-only: Development requests use their own session.

items.title: Statistics and Plans in their own folders
items.detail: Internal change; nothing changes in use.

items.title: The System page in its own folder
items.detail: Internal change; nothing changes in use.

items.title: The whole core in separate parts
items.detail: Internal change; nothing changes in use.

items.title: Web search and other tools per agent
items.detail: Each agent's tab has a “What the agent can do” list: web search, opening pages, running commands and more, where the agent supports them. Web search is on by default. Organizations can block each item.

items.title: What the agent said along the way stays collapsed
items.detail: Only the agent's latest message while working shows above the answer; a button opens the earlier ones.

items.title: "Unsaved changes" no longer pushes the buttons
items.detail: In Settings, the “Unsaved changes” notice no longer pushes the buttons down.

items.title: Projects, chats and Live in separate parts
items.detail: Internal change; nothing changes in use.

items.title: Code index and memory in separate parts
items.detail: Internal change; nothing changes in use.

items.title: Jev, plans and organizations in separate parts
items.detail: Internal change; nothing changes in use.

items.title: A request cut off by closing the app does not restart by itself
items.detail: A request cut off by closing the app now shows as failed, with a one-click resend, instead of restarting by itself. Queued requests stay in the queue.

items.title: Search sees what the agent just created
items.detail: After each Development request, the project is indexed again, so search sees new files.

items.title: Settings and System open while an agent works
items.detail: Settings and System now open right away while a request runs; changes apply from the next request.

items.title: A project in two organizations follows the stricter policy
items.detail: A project with repositories from two organizations now follows the stricter of their LLM policies.

items.title: Chat titles with command-line agents too
items.detail: Command-line agents now name chats too, with one short read-only call per chat.

items.title: Cloud and agents in separate parts
items.detail: Internal change; nothing changes in use.

items.title: Core foundation in separate parts
items.detail: Internal change; nothing changes in use.

items.title: Core organized in layers
items.detail: Internal change; nothing changes in use.

items.title: Plans and subscription
items.detail: The Plans page shows what each plan includes and lets you subscribe. Without a subscription, you stay on the free plan.

items.title: Features controlled by the administrator
items.detail: The administrator can now turn features on or off and include them in each plan.

items.title: The request queue no longer gets stuck
items.detail: Fixed cases where the request queue got stuck or sent queued messages out of order.

items.title: Nothing you type gets lost
items.detail: Fixed cases where typed text or unsaved settings were lost, and where a double click sent two answers.

items.title: Security fixes
items.detail: Several security fixes: stronger protection for the app's texts, file reading limited to the project folder, and retries no longer use up the quota.

items.title: Big requests split between agents working at the same time
items.detail: Turn on Split big requests between agents in Settings › Jev. Complex Development requests in a git project are split into up to 4 parts that different agents handle at the same time, and the changes come back to your folder.

items.title: A reasoning model plans, a coding agent builds
items.detail: Turn on Plan with one model, build with another in Settings › Jev. For complex Development requests, a strong reasoning model plans first and the building agent gets the plan.

items.title: Another agent reviews what the first one changed
items.detail: Turn on Second opinion from another agent in Settings › Jev. After a change, an agent from another provider reviews the diff and lists problems at the end of the answer.

items.title: Choose which agent wins a tie
items.detail: In Settings › Jev, Agent preference decides which agent answers when two score the same.

items.title: Small models no longer count as reasoning models
items.detail: Newly found small models no longer count as reasoning models, so they don't take complex requests. Models you already have keep your settings.

items.title: Jev uses every agent you configured
items.detail: When agents tie, a chat keeps its current agent and new chats are spread among the others. Untried models start with an average score, so Jev learns which agent works best for each kind of request.

items.title: If the chosen agent cannot start, the next one answers
items.detail: If the chosen agent isn't installed, can't start or isn't signed in, the request goes to the next agent and the answer says so.

items.title: Closing the window keeps the app running in the tray
items.detail: Closing the window now hides it; queued requests, sync and update checks keep running. Use the tray menu to reopen or quit the app.

items.title: New versions show up even with the window hidden
items.detail: Update checks now run even when the window is hidden.

items.title: The code panel follows the agent more reliably
items.detail: The code panel now shows more accurate diffs, no longer lists temporary files and no longer misses quick saves.

items.title: The chat filter in Statistics no longer stretches across the screen
items.detail: The project and chat filters in Statistics have a fixed width, and long chat titles are shortened.

items.title: Development mode edits files again
items.detail: In Development mode, agents can edit project files again; commands still follow your settings.

items.title: What changes shows only the new version
items.detail: In the update notice, What changes shows only what the new version brings, with a button to update.

items.title: Chat messages fit inside their bubble
items.detail: Long links and words now wrap inside the chat bubble, and wide tables and code scroll inside it.

items.title: Answering the agent is no longer blocked at the gatehouse
items.detail: Answering the agent's follow-up questions is no longer blocked at the gatehouse.

items.title: Easier-to-read code and file paths
items.detail: Code in answers is highlighted and has line numbers, and long blocks start collapsed. File paths show as badges with the file name highlighted.

items.title: Choose Planning or Development in each chat
items.detail: Each chat has a work mode: Auto, Planning or Development. Switch with /plan, /build or /auto, Ctrl+. or the command palette. Jev switches to Development when you ask to implement, with a button to undo.

items.title: Who said what, at a glance
items.detail: Your requests appear in a bubble on the right; answers appear in a frame that shows the agent, the model and the gate's verdict.

items.title: Only the latest steps while a request runs
items.detail: While a request runs, only the 3 latest steps show. A button opens the full list.

items.title: Readable answer buttons
items.detail: Answer buttons in the agent's questions are readable again in light and dark themes.

items.title: Every text in your language
items.detail: Some newer texts appeared in English. All texts now load in your language.

items.title: Updates found within seconds
items.detail: The app now checks for a new version every 15 seconds and shows a notice when one is out.

items.title: Request steps in your language
items.detail: The steps shown while a request runs are now in your language.

items.title: Watch the files the agent changes, live
items.detail: A panel beside the chat shows every file the request changes and its diff, updated as the agent writes. You can also follow the changes in your code editor. Files covered by privacy rules show only their name.

items.title: Repositories inside the organization chat
items.detail: The organization chat shows every repository in the organization folder with its branch, sync status, changed files and policy. The button is now called Open chat.

items.title: Choose how often to look for updates
items.detail: In Settings › App you can choose how often to check for updates and see when the last check happened.

items.title: Texts that were still in English
items.detail: The update window, the Close button and some sign-in messages are now translated.

items.title: A clearer System page
items.detail: The System page opens with a health panel showing the server and each agent's status, plus the version and the update check.

items.title: Copy diagnostics
items.detail: Copy diagnostics puts version, system, connection and agent details on the clipboard, without chat content, keys or tokens.

items.title: Agent in all repositories
items.detail: The organization chat button now takes you to the existing chat instead of opening a new one.

items.title: Project filters and search
items.detail: Filter projects by All, Personal or Organizations, and search them by name, folder or repository.

items.title: You choose when to update
items.detail: Checking for updates no longer installs on its own: you choose to update now or later.

items.title: Tidier organization page
items.detail: The organization page is tidier: settings moved to a gear icon, and going back is an arrow beside the name.

items.title: A terminal look
items.detail: The app now has a terminal look with a monospaced font. Each request and answer form one block, marked when the gatehouse asked or blocked.

items.title: Command palette (Ctrl+K / ⌘K)
items.detail: Press Ctrl+K (⌘K on Mac) on any screen to search pages, projects, chats and actions. Keyboard shortcuts also open the main screens, a new chat, the gatehouse and Settings.

items.title: Status bar
items.detail: A bar at the bottom shows sync status, the project folder, the gatehouse count and the version.

items.title: Less code in build mode
items.detail: In Development mode the agent writes less code, reusing what already exists. Validation, error handling, security and accessibility are never cut. Turn it off under Your level.

items.title: A symbol index of your project
items.detail: The app indexes where functions, types and classes are defined in your project, locally and without using tokens, so agents find code faster.

items.title: A project map at the start of each agent session
items.detail: In large projects, a new agent session gets a short map of the main folders, key files and entry points.

items.title: Symbol tools for agents (optional)
items.detail: An optional setting lets the agent look up definitions and usages in the symbol index instead of searching files. Run jayv bench to see if it pays off.

items.title: Project memory
items.detail: Project memory keeps short notes for the agent: how to test, where things are, what not to touch. They're sent once per session, and secrets are refused.

items.title: The gatehouse learns from your answers
items.detail: When you answer a gatehouse question in your next request, the answer becomes a project note, and the gatehouse won't ask it again.

items.title: Routing learns from what did not work
items.detail: If your next message says something didn't work, or the exit gate held the answer, the model loses a point. Scores are kept per kind of request.

items.title: Level suggestion
items.detail: Your level now suggests moving up or down when the last 30 days of gatehouse history call for it. Switching takes one click.

items.title: Search your chats
items.detail: Search what was said in a project's chats, with matches highlighted. It runs locally.

items.title: Reuses answers the project already has
items.detail: When a request is nearly identical to one already answered in the project, the earlier answer is reused as a starting point.

items.title: Recipes for requests you repeat
items.detail: Project memory shows requests you repeat and lets you turn them into recipes, sent only with matching requests.

items.title: Agents pick up where they left off
items.detail: In the same chat, the next request resumes the agent's previous session, so it doesn't reread the project on every message. A new session starts after 10 requests or when the agent, model or folder changes.

items.title: A file map instead of whole files
items.detail: Agents that read the project themselves now get a map of the most relevant files and open only what they need. Models used through an API still get the files.

items.title: Faster start for every request
items.detail: The entry gate and routing now run at the same time, so requests start faster.

items.title: Prompt cache for API models
items.detail: With models used through an API, the instructions and earlier messages use the prompt cache and are billed at the cached rate. Cached tokens now show in usage.

items.title: Measure the savings yourself
items.detail: The jayv bench command runs the same requests with and without the app and shows the tokens each one used, so you can measure the savings in your project.

items.title: Savings panel shows only real savings
items.detail: “Trimmed context” was removed from What it saved, since it didn't reflect real savings. Resumed agent sessions now show in What it did.

items.title: Chat titles no longer open an agent session
items.detail: Naming a chat no longer starts a full agent session. Only API models name chats; otherwise the chat keeps a summary of your first request.

items.title: Better choice of relevant files
items.detail: File search now favors rare words, splits names like fetchUserName, ignores filler words, ranks docs below code and sends the matching part of large files.

items.title: Shorter history in each request
items.detail: When the agent session can't be resumed, earlier answers are shortened in the history to save tokens.

items.title: What's new window
items.detail: After each update, this window shows what changed, split into new features and fixes. It appears once per version.

items.title: Version history anytime
items.detail: Settings › App › Version has a What's new button that reopens this window with the full history.

items.title: Sidebar and header stay put when scrolling
items.detail: The sidebar and header now stay in place while the page content scrolls.

items.title: Organization chat across every repository
items.detail: The organization page has an Organization chat button that opens one chat working on all its repositories, using the organization folder on this computer.

items.title: See which repositories join the chat
items.detail: Before opening the organization chat, a window shows which repositories are included and which are left out, and why.

items.title: The strictest policy applies in the organization chat
items.detail: The organization chat follows the strictest LLM policy of the organization and its repositories.

items.title: Organization chat in Statistics and Gate
items.detail: Usage from the organization chat now shows right away in the organization's Statistics and Gatehouse tabs.

items.title: Two-factor authentication
items.detail: Turn on an authenticator app: scan the QR code and confirm with the first code.

items.title: A 6-digit code at every sign-in
items.detail: With two-factor on, every sign-in asks for the 6-digit code.

items.title: Turning protection off asks for a code
items.detail: Turning off two-factor requires a current code from the app; an open session isn't enough.

items.title: Changing the password with the app on
items.detail: With two-factor on, changing your password also asks for the app code.

items.title: Installed app closed to inspection
items.detail: In the installed app, the right-click menu (except in text fields) and the shortcuts for developer tools, view source, save, print and reload are turned off.

items.title: Safer connections
items.detail: All connections now require TLS 1.2 or newer and trust only built-in certificate authorities. Proxies that intercept HTTPS are refused.

items.title: Real-time notifications are back
items.detail: Real-time notifications work again, and the two-factor QR code shows correctly.

items.title: Statistics tab in the organization
items.detail: The organization's Statistics tab adds up usage from its projects on this computer, with project, chat and period filters.

items.title: Gate tab in the organization
items.detail: The organization's Gatehouse tab shows the entry and exit gates for its projects, with the same filters as Statistics.

items.title: Username set once
items.detail: Your username is locked after you first save your profile. The form warns you before saving.

items.title: New organizations start with a policy
items.detail: New organizations start with safe privacy defaults, and the policy opens ready to adjust.

items.title: Updated agent icons
items.detail: The agent tabs now show the current official icons.

items.title: Executable field locked
items.detail: For built-in agents, the app sets the executable and the field is locked; Check still works.

items.title: New version notice at the top
items.detail: When a new version is out, a bar at the top shows What changes and Update now. Closing it hides the notice for that version.

items.title: New version in the bell too
items.detail: Each new version also appears once in the notifications and opens the update window.

items.title: Updates no longer interrupt your work
items.detail: The update check no longer installs right away: it notifies you, and you choose when to update.

items.title: Remove the organization folder
items.detail: In the Repositories tab, Remove makes this computer forget the organization folder. Nothing is deleted.

items.title: Deleting a project removes its chats everywhere
items.detail: Deleting a project now removes its chats on all your computers.
